subject: redPanda
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: red panda balancing on a mossy stone.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact design for a red panda standing in a resting quadruped pose on a mossy stone, Genshin cel-shaded style, working out realistic proportions for the body, tail, and stone footprint to keep things grounded before building out the model.

Now I'm setting up the skeleton and geometry: the stone's top defines the ground plane, with hip and spine joints positioned above it, a looped spine chain, neck, head, jaw, and tail joints, plus limb chains for the legs using the toon kit's cel-shading, fur edges, and anime eye decals. For the head I'm shaping a wide skull sphere with a small cream muzzle, nose, rounded ears, eye decals, cheek ruffs, and painted facial markings to get that distinctive red panda face.

Continuing the coloring, I'm texturing rust-colored skulls, white muzzle and cheek regions, and flattened ears with cream inner discs. For the legs, I'm darkening them toward the paws with a gradient paint and setting up two-segment limb chains with appropriate bend directions for front and hind legs, plus small flattened foot spheres at the tips.

Writing tail chain code...

Now I'm sizing the stone base with a radius around 0.3 positioned so the tail hangs safely above it, then building the stone as a lathed profile with moss patches painted on upward-facing normals.

Adjusting foot positions slightly so they sink naturally into the stone surface, keeping the pose neutral rather than raised. For the face, I'm placing amber iris eyes via surface decals near the muzzle, adding a small black nose sphere, and building a cream scaled muzzle with a small jaw part underneath for the mouth.

Now I'm shaping the jaw as a scaled sphere attached to the jaw joint, and scattering fur tuft cards across the body in rust tones (around 150 instances) plus cream cheek ruffs. I'm also working out the skeleton chain for the neck and head, positioning joints so the neck connects the chest end to the head center with proper direction vectors.

For coloring, I'm using a cel-shaded fur edge paint to give the body a rust-to-dark-brown transition for countershading, solid dark brown for the legs, and a separate ring pattern function for the tail that alternates between two colors based on position along its length.

For the ears, I'm shaping small scaled spheres oriented outward along the ear axis, with a rust-colored outer shell and a slightly smaller cream disc positioned forward to mimic the characteristic red panda ear rim coloring.

Now I'm adding cream dots above the eyes for eyebrows and considering tear marks as dark rust shapes running down from the eyes, then scattering green moss blobs around the stone rim using a ring placement pattern, with moss tufts layered in for texture while skipping extra flourishes like flowers or glow effects. I'm also noting the limb-building function takes root/target points, length arrays, and bend parameters.

For the front leg I'm working out the geometry—checking that the distance between root and foot matches the sum of segment lengths, and adjusting the body's vertical position and height so the short legs characteristic of a red panda still reach the ground properly with believable bend angles.

Still defining the leg and spine geometry...

Now I'm placing the head: skull sphere, cream muzzle and nose spheres, and a jaw joint aimed toward the muzzle with its own cream jaw piece. I'm skipping the mouth detail and starting on cheek ruffs, scattering cream tufts across the skull surface filtered to the outer cheek region.

I'm sizing and leaning those cheek tuft cards, then setting up eye decals mirrored on each side using surface hits around the skull, with a guard in case a hit comes back null.
